newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toray to boost output of airbag nylon.
newsitem.headline: Toray to boost output of airbag nylon.

text.p: Toray Industries Inc said on Monday it plans to invest two billion yen to expand domestic production facilities for nylon 66, used in car airbags, in order to meet growing domestic demand.

The new facilities at Toray's Okazaki plant, in Aichi Prefecture in central Japan, will boost its production of nylon 66 for airbag applications to 600 tonnes per month from 280 tonnes at present, the company said. The new facilities will start operations in April 1998.

Japanese carmakers are increasingly installing airbags as standard equipment for driver's seats and front passenger seats. Nearly all domestic cars are expected to be equipped with airbags by the year 2000.
Toray supplies nylon 66 to all Japanese carmakers for airbags.
Annual demand for Toray's airbag nylon fibre is expected to rise to about 9,000 tonnes by the year 2000 from 4,000 tonnes in 1996, the company said.
